clue.text: Teenager showing sense after a grant is made

indicators.note: after places the word for sense behind the a-plus-grant pair

parts.note: the dole is a state benefit, a grant of money to the unemployed
scent is a sense, as in a dog's scent for a trail

explanation.surface: A youngster acquires good sense once some money has been handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: DOLE is the British word for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person in the years between childhood and adulthood, just as a teenager is.

clue.text: Involved in one-sided rows, eventually nod

indicators.note: involved in means the answer is wrapped up within the next run of words

explanation.surface: Unbalanced arguments eventually make a listener nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in 'one-sideD ROWS Eventually'.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze is to nod off, dropping one's head while half-asleep.

clue.text: Praise a 50% reduction in figure using a drug

parts.note: to laud is to praise

indicators.note: a 50% reduction removes half the letters of the word for figure

parts.note: a figure is a number

explanation.surface: Someone uses a drug to lose half their figure.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% reduction in' halves NUMBER to NUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudanum is a tincture of opium, once a common narcotic medicine.

clue.text: The way issue's taken about single mother becoming a manual worker

indicators.note: taken about means the pair of way and issue go around the next pieces

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a son is issue, offspring
one means single
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A single mother's son takes up building work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken about' wraps the way-plus-issue pair round single-plus-mother; ST is street, a crossword staple for 'way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason cuts and lays stone by hand, a skilled trade done with the hands.

clue.text: American naval officers sensing mutiny

indicators.note: a mutiny is a revolt that turns things over, so the letters of sensing are rearranged

explanation.surface: Junior US Navy officers sense the crew is about to mutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutiny' rearranges SENSING.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US Navy the most junior commissioned rank is ensign.

clue.text: Drop and damage

explanation.surface: Something falls and gets broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop falls from the eye, and to rip cloth is to cause damage.

clue.text: The person, at the bank is a landowner

definitions.text: The person, at the bank is a landowner

parts.words: The person, at the bank is a landowner
parts.note: the bank suggests money, but it is a riverbank: the word names one who owns land beside a river

explanation.surface: Someone at the bank turns out to be a man of property.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank is a riverbank, not a financial one.
explanation.definitionFit: A riparian owner holds property along the edge of a river or stream.

clue.text: Posted a note in payment for accommodation, giving offence

indicators.note: in puts the posted note inside the payment for accommodation

parts.note: rent is what a tenant pays for accommodation
posted means sent, as with a letter
me is a note in sol-fa, often spelt mi

explanation.surface: A tenant sends a note with the payment and causes upset.
explanation.walkthrough: ME (also spelt mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking offence is feeling aggrieved bitterness, which is what resentment is.

clue.text: Conservationists in Ireland are not divided

indicators.note: in tells us the conservationists sit inside the name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation body

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners in Ireland stand united.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust (NT) looks after historic buildings and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undivided is complete, all in one piece.

clue.text: "Hell is a city much like London — a ______ and smoky city." (Shelley)

definitions.text: "Hell is a city much like London — a ______ and smoky city." (Shelley)

parts.words: "Hell is a city much like London — a ______ and smoky city." (Shelley)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing adjective describes a crowded city, from Shelley's Peter Bell the Third

explanation.walkthrough: This is a quotation clue: supply the missing word from Shelley's line comparing Hell to crowded, smoky London.
explanation.definitionFit: A city packed with many inhabitants is densely peopled, which is what London was to Shelley.

clue.text: Anger — anger about nasty trait

indicators.note: about means the word for anger goes around the other letters

parts.note: ire is a literary word for anger

indicators.note: nasty suggests the letters of trait are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Fury builds over someone's unpleasant characteristic.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word is the setter's: the first 'Anger' is the verb defined, the second supplies the wordplay; 'nasty' gives RITAT, which 'about' encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate someone is to annoy or provoke them, here used as a verb.

clue.text: All four corners must be stitched

parts.note: south is one of the four compass points, the corners of the earth
east is another compass point
west is another compass point
north completes the four compass points

explanation.surface: A tailor insists every corner of the garment be sewn up.
explanation.walkthrough: The four corners are the compass points S, E, W, N, a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn is the past participle of sew, so the material has been joined with needle and thread.

clue.text: Old member of the crew after support

indicators.note: after places the crew member behind the word for support

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a hand is a member of a ship's crew

explanation.surface: A veteran sailor comes after the backing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' here means used before, as of goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that have had a previous owner are used, not new.

clue.text: She is given a hand when she starts work

definitions.text: She is given a hand when she starts work

parts.words: She is given a hand when she starts work
parts.note: reads like applause for a performer, but the hand is the customer's, offered for nail care

explanation.surface: A performer is applauded as she begins her act.
explanation.definitionFit: A beautician who tends fingernails must hold each client's hand to begin her job.

clue.text: The transferring of property or vehicle

explanation.surface: A legal document deals with moving property, perhaps a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Conveyancing is the legal transfer of property title, and the word also means any means of transport.

clue.text: A drug-dealer who may well have scruples

definitions.text: A drug-dealer who may well have scruples

parts.words: A drug-dealer who may well have scruples
parts.note: scruples are both moral qualms and an old apothecaries' unit of weight, used by a pharmacist dispensing drugs

explanation.surface: Even a narcotics pusher might have a conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: A scruple was a small apothecaries' weight of twenty grains, so a pharmacist would literally keep scruples.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist in a shop legally dispenses medicines, so is a dealer in drugs.

clue.text: The egghead never accepts a drink, being a constructive man

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E

indicators.note: accepts means the word for never takes the drink inside it

parts.note: ne'er is a poetic contraction of never
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A teetotal intellectual refuses a drink, being of practical mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives E, the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineer designs and builds machines and structures, so is someone who constructs things.

clue.text: Sent in wrong direction, becomes violent

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the words sent in are put in a new order

parts.note: E for east is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone sent the wrong way turns aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges SENTIN to INTENS, then E (east) is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something extreme in force or strength, as in a fierce storm.

clue.text: Around here getting up late can be heavenly!

indicators.note: around means the turned word goes around the other piece
getting up in a down clue means the word late is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Lying in bed late around here can feel divine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'getting up' reverses, giving ETAL; 'Around' means that reversed word encloses the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means airy and otherworldly, of the heavens rather than the earth.

clue.text: Called for as arranged

explanation.surface: Something was requested exactly as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordered means requested or demanded, and also set out tidily in sequence.

clue.text: The woman tending to help one through dark times

definitions.text: The woman tending to help one through dark times

parts.words: The woman tending to help one through dark times
parts.note: dark times sounds like depression or grief, but it means the literal hours of darkness on a hospital ward

explanation.surface: A kind woman supports someone through a bleak period of life.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital carer on the late shift looks after patients through the hours of darkness.

clue.text: A crowd entertainer

explanation.surface: A performer who draws a large audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great multitude, as in a host of angels, and also the one who receives guests at a party.

clue.text: Quiet leftists making cuts

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
reds are left-wingers, communists

explanation.surface: Silent left-wing activists slash budgets.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred is to cut or tear into thin strips.

clue.text: Beautiful homes — and otherwise!

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in another way, so the letters of homes and and are shuffled

explanation.surface: An estate agent praises lovely houses, then hints at the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges HOMES and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome means good-looking or attractive, a near synonym of beautiful.

clue.text: Love the German for "river'!

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written as O
der is German for the

explanation.surface: Someone loves the German word for river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oder is a river on the German-Polish border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a major central European waterway flowing to the Baltic.

clue.text: Turned over and faced the wall

explanation.surface: A builder flipped something and then plastered the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: To render a wall is to coat it with plaster or cement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered means handed over or surrendered, and also coated a wall's surface with a layer of plaster.

clue.text: This could be put on record as 11

definitions.text: This could be put on record

explanation.surface: A remark could be noted officially as provocation.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the answer to 11 across, IRRITATE; the first sense is a gramophone stylus placed on a vinyl record.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is lowered on to a spinning disc to play it, and to goad or provoke someone is the verb sense.

clue.text: Lacking guidance, dug in right' and left with Oriental craft

indicators.note: in shows the word for dug is placed between the letters for right and left

parts.note: a dug is an animal's teat or udder
E for East stands for Oriental
SS, steamship, is a craft

explanation.surface: A rudderless soul digs in on both sides with an Eastern boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug' is a noun here, an animal's teat, not the past of dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat without its steering blade drifts aimlessly, so the word means without direction.
